_readme: Built-in monsters for Stage 4. Loaded when the server starts; edit here and redeploy.
age: Archaic, Classical or Heroic. difficulty_factor: the monster's max roll = alliance points x this (defaults: Archaic 0.25, Classical 0.50, Heroic 0.75).
matchups: god key -> effective (monster's max roll -35%) or resisted (no reduction). Gods not listed are neutral (-15%). Tune in Test Period.
win_points / lose_points: like Fate battles (lose_points is negative).
passage + questions: the battle shows the passage and asks 3 of the questions (one try each; each right answer raises the alliance's max roll by 10%).
The passages below are ORIGINAL short retellings written for this game.

monsters.name: Typhon
monsters.passage: When the young gods had defeated the Titans, Gaia, the Earth, was angry that her children had been thrown into Tartarus. From the deepest pits she brought out Typhon, the last and largest of her sons. His head brushed the stars, and a hundred serpent heads hissed from his shoulders. Fire poured from his eyes. Many of the Olympians fled in fear, but Zeus stood and fought. After a long battle, he struck Typhon again and again with his thunderbolts and buried him under Mount Etna, where, the Greeks said, he still breathes fire.

questions.prompt: Why did Gaia bring Typhon out of the pits?
options: She was angry that her children were thrown into Tartarus
She wanted Typhon to guard Olympus
Typhon was lost and wanted to go home

questions.prompt: What does "brushed the stars" tell the reader about Typhon?
How is Zeus different from many of the other Olympians in this passage?
What everyday thing does the last sentence explain?

monsters.name: Cerberus
monsters.passage: At the gates of the Underworld waits Cerberus, a dog with three heads and a serpent for a tail. He lets the dead walk in, but he lets no one walk out, and no living person may pass him at all. When Orpheus came to bring back Eurydice, he did not fight the hound. He sat on a stone and played his lyre. The music was so sweet and sad that all three heads lowered, one after another, until Cerberus lay down and let him through.

questions.prompt: What is Cerberus's job?
options: to carry the dead across the river
to guard the gates so no one leaves the Underworld
to judge the souls of the dead

questions.prompt: How does Orpheus get past Cerberus?
options: He fights him with a sword
He plays music on his lyre
He sneaks past while the dog sleeps

questions.prompt: The phrase "one after another" shows that the heads lowered
What does the passage suggest about Orpheus's music?
options: It could calm even a monster
It was too loud to bear

monsters.name: The Minotaur
monsters.passage: Beneath the palace of King Minos, Daedalus built the Labyrinth, a maze so twisting that whoever entered could never find the way out. In its center lived the Minotaur, half man and half bull. Every nine years Athens had to send fourteen young people to be fed to it. Theseus, son of the king of Athens, chose to go with them. Princess Ariadne gave him a ball of thread. He tied one end at the entrance, unwound it as he walked, killed the Minotaur, and followed the thread back to the light.

questions.prompt: Why could no one escape the Labyrinth?
options: Its walls were made of fire
It was a maze too twisting to find the way out

questions.prompt: What does Theseus's choice to go with the young Athenians show about him?
options: He was brave and willing to protect others

questions.prompt: How did the thread help Theseus?
options: He used it to tie up the Minotaur
It showed him the way back out
It was a gift to sell

questions.prompt: How is the passage organized?
options: problem, then how a hero solves it
a list of facts about bulls

monsters.name: Medusa
monsters.passage: Medusa had snakes for hair, and anyone who looked into her eyes turned to stone. Her cave was full of statues that had once been warriors. When Perseus was sent to bring back her head, the gods helped him. Hermes lent him winged sandals, and Athena gave him a polished shield. Perseus never looked at Medusa directly. He watched her reflection in the shield, crept close while she slept, and struck.

questions.prompt: Why was the cave full of statues?
options: They were warriors turned to stone

questions.prompt: Why did Perseus look at Medusa's reflection?
options: so he would not meet her eyes and turn to stone
because the cave was too dark

questions.prompt: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Perseus used the gods' gifts and cleverness to defeat Medusa
Medusa was lonely in her cave

questions.prompt: In this passage, "crept" most nearly means

monsters.name: The Hydra
monsters.passage: In the swamps of Lerna lived the Hydra, a serpent with many heads. Its breath was poison, and when Heracles cut off one head, two grew back in its place. Fighting alone, he could not win. So his nephew Iolaus brought a torch, and each time Heracles cut off a head, Iolaus burned the stump so nothing could grow back. Together they defeated the monster that neither could have beaten alone.

questions.prompt: What made the Hydra so hard to defeat?
options: Two heads grew back for every one cut off

questions.prompt: What does the passage suggest about teamwork?
options: Working together can solve a problem one person cannot
Only gods can work as a team

questions.prompt: Why did Iolaus burn each stump?
options: so no new heads could grow back

questions.prompt: Where did the Hydra live?
options: in a cave by the sea
